+/*
+** Return the length (in bytes) of a utf-8 character.  Or return a maximum
+** of N.
+*/
+static int utf8Len(unsigned char c, int N){
+  int len = 1;
+  if( c>0x7f ){
+    if( (c&0xe0)==0xc0 ){
+      len = 2;
+    }else if( (c&0xf0)==0xe0 ){
+      len = 3;
+    }else{
+      len = 4;
+    }
+  }
+  if( len>N ) len = N;
+  return len;
+}
+
+/*
+** Return TRUE (non-zero) of the To side of the given cost matches
+** the given string.
+*/
+static int matchTo(EditDist3Cost *p, const char *z, int n){
+  if( p->nTo>n ) return 0;
+  if( memcmp(p->a+p->nFrom, z, p->nTo)!=0 ) return 0;
+  return 1;
+}
+
+/*
+** Return TRUE (non-zero) of the To side of the given cost matches
+** the given string.
+*/
+static int matchFrom(EditDist3Cost *p, const char *z, int n){
+  if( p->nFrom>n ) return 0;
+  if( memcmp(p->a, z, p->nFrom)!=0 ) return 0;
+  return 1;
+}
+
+/*
+** Return TRUE (non-zero) of the next FROM character and the next TO
+** character are the same.
+*/
+static int matchFromTo(
+  EditDist3FromString *pStr,  /* Left hand string */
+  int n1,                     /* Index of comparison character on the left */
+  const char *z2,             /* Right-handl comparison character */
+  int n2                      /* Bytes remaining in z2[] */
+){
+  int b1 = pStr->a[n1].nByte;
+  if( b1>n2 ) return 0;
+  if( memcmp(pStr->z+n1, z2, b1)!=0 ) return 0;
+  return 1;
+}
+
+/*
+** Delete an EditDist3FromString objecct
+*/
+static void editDist3FromStringDelete(EditDist3FromString *p){
+  int i;
+  if( p ){
+    for(i=0; i<p->n; i++){
+      sqlite3_free(p->a[i].apDel);
+      sqlite3_free(p->a[i].apSubst);
+    }
+    sqlite3_free(p);
+  }
+}
+
+/*
+** Create a EditDist3FromString object.
+*/
+static EditDist3FromString *editDist3FromStringNew(
+  const EditDist3Lang *pLang,
+  const char *z,
+  int n
+){
+  EditDist3FromString *pStr;
+  EditDist3Cost *p;
+  int i;
+
+  if( n<0 ) n = (int)strlen(z);
+  pStr = sqlite3_malloc( sizeof(*pStr) + sizeof(pStr->a[0])*n + n + 1 );
+  if( pStr==0 ) return 0;
+  pStr->a = (EditDist3From*)&pStr[1];
+  pStr->n = n;
+  pStr->z = (char*)&pStr->a[n];
+  memcpy(pStr->z, z, n+1);
+  if( n && z[n-1]=='*' ){
+    pStr->isPrefix = 1;
+    n--;
+    pStr->n--;
+    pStr->z[n] = 0;
+  }else{
+    pStr->isPrefix = 0;
+  }
+
+  for(i=0; i<n; i++){
+    EditDist3From *pFrom = &pStr->a[i];
+    memset(pFrom, 0, sizeof(*pFrom));
+    pFrom->nByte = utf8Len((unsigned char)z[i], n-i);
+    for(p=pLang->pCost; p; p=p->pNext){
+      EditDist3Cost **apNew;
+      if( i+p->nFrom>n ) continue;
+      if( matchFrom(p, z+i, n-i)==0 ) continue;
+      if( p->nTo==0 ){
+        apNew = sqlite3_realloc(pFrom->apDel,
+                                sizeof(*apNew)*(pFrom->nDel+1));
+        if( apNew==0 ) break;
+        pFrom->apDel = apNew;
+        apNew[pFrom->nDel++] = p;
+      }else{
+        apNew = sqlite3_realloc(pFrom->apSubst,
+                                sizeof(*apNew)*(pFrom->nSubst+1));
+        if( apNew==0 ) break;
+        pFrom->apSubst = apNew;
+        apNew[pFrom->nSubst++] = p;
+      }
+    }
+    if( p ){
+      editDist3FromStringDelete(pStr);
+      pStr = 0;
+      break;
+    }
+  }
+  return pStr;
+}

+/*
+** Return the number of bytes in the common prefix of two UTF8 strings.
+** Only complete characters are considered.
+*/
+static int editDist3PrefixLen(const char *z1, const char *z2){
+  int n = 0;
+  while( z1[n] && z1[n]==z2[n] ){ n++; }
+  while( n && (z1[n]&0xc0)==0x80 ){ n--; }
+  return n;
+}
+
+/*
+** Return the number of bytes in the common suffix of two UTF8 strings.
+** Only complete characters are considered.
+*/
+static int editDist3SuffixLen(const char *z1, int n1, const char *z2, int n2){
+  int origN1 = n1;
+  while( n1>0 && n2>0 && z1[n1-1]==z2[n2-1] ){ n1--; n2--; }
+  while( n1<origN1 && (z1[n1]&0xc0)==0x80 ){ n1++; n2++; }
+  return origN1 - n1;
+}

+/*
+** Update entry m[i] such that it is the minimum of its current value
+** and m[j]+iCost.
+**
+** If the iCost is 1,000,000 or greater, then consider the cost to be
+** infinite and skip the update.
+*/
+static void updateCost(
+  unsigned int *m,
+  int i,
+  int j,
+  int iCost
+){
+  int b;
+  if( iCost<10000 ){
+    b = m[j] + iCost;
+    if( b<m[i] ) m[i] = b;
+  }
+}

+/*
+** Function:    editdist3(A,B,iLang)
+**              editdist3(tablename)
+**
+** Return the cost of transforming string A into string B using edit
+** weights for iLang.
+**
+** The second form loads edit weights into memory from a table.
+*/
+static void editDist3SqlFunc(
+  sqlite3_context *context,
+  int argc,
+  sqlite3_value **argv
+){
+  EditDist3Config *pConfig = (EditDist3Config*)sqlite3_user_data(context);
+  sqlite3 *db = sqlite3_context_db_handle(context);
+  int rc;
+  if( argc==1 ){
+    const char *zTable = (const char*)sqlite3_value_text(argv[0]);
+    rc = editDist3ConfigLoad(pConfig, db, zTable);
+    if( rc ) sqlite3_result_error_code(context, rc);
+  }else{
+    const char *zA = (const char*)sqlite3_value_text(argv[0]);
+    const char *zB = (const char*)sqlite3_value_text(argv[1]);
+    int nA = sqlite3_value_bytes(argv[0]);
+    int nB = sqlite3_value_bytes(argv[1]);
+    int iLang = argc==3 ? sqlite3_value_int(argv[2]) : 0;
+    const EditDist3Lang *pLang = editDist3FindLang(pConfig, iLang);
+    EditDist3FromString *pFrom;
+    int dist;
+
+    pFrom = editDist3FromStringNew(pLang, zA, nA);
+    if( pFrom==0 ){
+      sqlite3_result_error_nomem(context);
+      return;
+    }
+    dist = editDist3Core(pFrom, zB, nB, pLang);
+    editDist3FromStringDelete(pFrom);
+    if( dist==(-1) ){
+      sqlite3_result_error_nomem(context);
+    }else if( dist==(-2) ){
+      sqlite3_result_error_toobig(context);
+    }else{
+      sqlite3_result_int(context, dist);
+    }
+  } 
+}

+/*
+** Register the editDist3 function with SQLite
+*/
+static int editDist3Install(sqlite3 *db){
+  int rc;
+  EditDist3Config *pConfig = sqlite3_malloc( sizeof(*pConfig) );
+  if( pConfig==0 ) return SQLITE_NOMEM;
+  memset(pConfig, 0, sizeof(*pConfig));
+  rc = sqlite3_create_function_v2(db, "editdist3",
+              2, SQLITE_UTF8, pConfig, editDist3SqlFunc, 0, 0, 0);
+  if( rc==SQLITE_OK ){
+    rc = sqlite3_create_function_v2(db, "editdist3",
+                3, SQLITE_UTF8, pConfig, editDist3SqlFunc, 0, 0, 0);
+  }
+  if( rc==SQLITE_OK ){
+    rc = sqlite3_create_function_v2(db, "editdist3",
+                1, SQLITE_UTF8, pConfig, editDist3SqlFunc, 0, 0,
+                editDist3ConfigDelete);
+  }else{
+    sqlite3_free(pConfig);
+  }
+  return rc;
+}

intro_commit_message:
Update test_spellfix.c with latest changes.

FossilOrigin-Name: cba2a65870481df213e006b07e74f0ca19d2d57c
pr_description:
Update the spellfix extension with the latest edit-distance functionality. Limit FROM and TO lengths to 10,000 before sizing the Wagner matrix, and report oversized inputs and allocation failures through SQLite errors.

Validated ordinary input, both 10,000-byte boundaries, oversized inputs on either side, and a pair of 47,000-byte strings. Workspace validation passes.
pr_title: Update spellfix with bounded edit-distance inputs
release_caveats: Actual Git committer date predates 2021: conflicts with current paper. Recommend explicitly removing/excepting introduction-age cutoff, keeping fixing-date window.

findings.message: In editDist3Core(), the Wagner-Fischer edit-distance matrix dimensions are computed as 'n = (f.n+1)*(n2+1)' where both f.n (FROM string length) and n2 (TO string length) are plain 'int' values with no upper-bound guard. When an attacker supplies two sufficiently long strings to the editdist3() SQL function, the multiplication overflows a 32-bit signed integer, yielding a small or negative value for n. The subsequent heap allocation 'nByte = n*sizeof(m[0]) + sizeof(a2[0])*n2' is then based on the corrupted n, so sqlite3_malloc64() allocates a far-too-small buffer; all subsequent matrix writes overflow that buffer, corrupting the heap. Even without a full overflow, the O(m×n) algorithm imposes unbounded CPU time for arbitrarily large inputs. The fix adds explicit guards 'if( n2>10000 ) return -2; if( f.n>10000 ) return -2;' before the matrix size computation.

related_locations.description: User-controlled SQL arguments zA/zB with lengths nA/nB are passed without size validation into editDist3FromStringNew() and editDist3Core(), allowing unbounded-length inputs to reach the vulnerable computation.

findings.suggestion: Add input size guards before the matrix size computation in editDist3Core(). The fix adds: 'if( n2>10000 ) return -2;' and 'if( f.n>10000 ) return -2;' immediately before 'n = (f.n+1)*(n2+1);', and handles the new return code -2 in the caller (editDist3SqlFunc) as sqlite3_result_error_toobig().
findings.title: Integer overflow in Wagner-Fischer matrix size computation in editDist3Core()

fix_commit.message: Limit the size of input strings to the (disused) spellfix extension to avoid excessive runtime and integer overflows. [bugs:/forumpost/24a33e5d10|Bugs report 24a33e5d10].

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Integer overflow in Wagner-Fischer matrix size computation in editDist3Core()
Related location for: Integer overflow in Wagner-Fischer matrix size computation in editDist3Core()

ground_truth.root_cause: No upper-bound validation is applied to the FROM or TO string lengths before performing the integer multiplication used to size the edit-distance matrix. Both f.n and n2 are 32-bit signed integers, so their product can overflow when each exceeds roughly 46,000 characters, yielding a corrupted allocation size.

agent_reasoning: The fix commit changes a single call site in src/vdbesort.c: `szKeyInfo = SZ_KEYINFO(pCsr->pKeyInfo->nKeyField+1);` becomes `szKeyInfo = SZ_KEYINFO(pCsr->pKeyInfo->nKeyField);`. This removes the stray `+1` that caused an over-read past the end of the source KeyInfo struct during memcpy. I applied exactly this one-line edit, matching the fix commit, with no other changes.
commit_message:
Make use of the flexible-array feature of C99, when available, to try to pacify -fsanitize=strict-bounds.  This check-in fixes the core. There is more yet to do in FTS3, RTREE, and in FTS5.

findings.message:
While refactoring VdbeSorter/KeyInfo to use C99 flexible array members, the size computation for the KeyInfo object that is embedded/copied after the VdbeSorter struct was changed from `sizeof(KeyInfo) + (nKeyField-1)*sizeof(CollSeq*)` to `SZ_KEYINFO(nKeyField+1)`, where `SZ_KEYINFO(N)` is defined as `offsetof(KeyInfo,aColl) + (N)*sizeof(CollSeq*)`. Because `KeyInfo.aColl` is now a flexible array (rather than a 1-element array whose first slot was already accounted for by `sizeof(KeyInfo)`), the correct size for `nKeyField` collating-sequence pointers is `SZ_KEYINFO(nKeyField)`. Passing `nKeyField+1` allocates and copies room for one extra `CollSeq*` slot than actually exists in the source `KeyInfo` object pointed to by `pCsr->pKeyInfo`.

Later, `sqlite3VdbeSorterInit()` calls `memcpy(pKeyInfo, pCsr->pKeyInfo, szKeyInfo)`, copying `szKeyInfo` bytes from `pCsr->pKeyInfo`, which is only sized for `nKeyField` entries. Since `szKeyInfo` was computed as if there were `nKeyField+1` entries, the memcpy reads past the end of the `pCsr->pKeyInfo` allocation, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read (confirmed by ASan; particularly visible when `SQLITE_DEFAULT_MEMSTATUS=0` removes extra allocator padding that normally masked the overread).
findings.suggestion: Compute szKeyInfo using the actual number of key fields, not nKeyField+1, since SZ_KEYINFO(N) with the new flexible-array-based offsetof formula already accounts for exactly N CollSeq* slots (unlike the old sizeof(KeyInfo)+(N-1)*sizeof(CollSeq*) formula which needed the -1 adjustment because sizeof(KeyInfo) already included one slot).
findings.suggestion_code:
szKeyInfo = SZ_KEYINFO(pCsr->pKeyInfo->nKeyField);
sz = SZ_VDBESORTER(nWorker+1);

fix_commit.message: Fix an off-by-one error in the size computation of a vdbe-sorter. [forum:/forumpost/c1cc8b057a|Forum post c1cc8b057a]. Problem introduced by checkin [d4307a0d43f42e96].

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Off-by-one under-computation of KeyInfo buffer size causes heap OOB read in sqlite3VdbeSorterInit

ground_truth.root_cause: A macro semantics change (from a 'size for N-1 extra elements beyond the first embedded one' formula to a 'size for exactly N elements from offsetof' formula) was not reflected correctly at one of its call sites; the call site retained an extra '+1' meant for the old formula, causing the size computation to request one more array element than actually exists in the source object being copied.

pr_description: FossilOrigin-Name: 6fd6b32d06bd6a705e5140cd613af823b8183a6f6a9ceeeedfcf5e8b50821d68
pr_title: Make use of the flexible-array feature of C99, when available, to try to pacify -fsanitize=strict-bounds.  This check-in fixes the core. There is more yet to do in FTS3, RTREE, and in FTS5.

agent_reasoning: Without this change, FTS3/4 tables created in an untrusted schema (e.g. attached databases, or when SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA is off) could be used to indirectly invoke SQL functions flagged SQLITE_FUNC_DIRECT/SQLITE_FUNC_UNSAFE, because the module's own internally-generated SQL (built from schema-derived strings like column/table names and prepared as fresh top-level statements) was indistinguishable from trusted user SQL to the enforcement checks, which only recognized nested sub-parses (pParse->pToplevel!=0) or expressions parsed directly from DDL text (EP_FromDDL/fg.fromDDL). This let schema-controlled content smuggle calls to otherwise-restricted "unsafe" functions, defeating the purpose of marking FTS3/4 as SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS. The fix closes the gap by introducing SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL and having FTS3/4 set it on every internal sqlite3_prepare_v3() call via sqlite3Fts3PrepareStmt(), and by having the three risk-check sites also honor pParse->prepFlags & SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL, so these internal statements are now correctly subject to the trusted-schema restriction.
commit_message:
Enable SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS for FTS3, FTS5, and RTREE.

FossilOrigin-Name: f34c533b6c1f8ef3f69c75c1039406c12751cdde1fbdcb4d9776b24455facf8a

files.diff:
diff --git a/src/sqlite.h.in b/src/sqlite.h.in
index 54192422d6..e48eb96a44 100644
--- a/src/sqlite.h.in
+++ b/src/sqlite.h.in
@@ -4156,25 +4156,33 @@ int sqlite3_limit(sqlite3*, int id, int newVal);
 ** to be required for any prepared statement that wanted to use the
 ** [sqlite3_normalized_sql()] interface.  However, the
 ** [sqlite3_normalized_sql()] interface is now available to all
 ** prepared statements, regardless of whether or not they use this
 ** flag.
 **
 ** [[SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB]] <dt>SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB</dt>
 ** <dd>The SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB flag causes the SQL compiler
 ** to return an error (error code SQLITE_ERROR) if the statement uses
 ** any virtual tables.
+**
+** [[SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL]] <dt>SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL</dt>
+** <dd>The SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL causes the SQL compiler to behave as if
+** the SQL statement was part of a database schema. This only makes a
+** difference if the SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA option is set to off.
+** This flag may be used by virtual table implementations that do not
+** completely control the SQL commands that they evaluate.
 ** </dl>
 */
 #define SQLITE_PREPARE_PERSISTENT              0x01
 #define SQLITE_PREPARE_NORMALIZE               0x02
 #define SQLITE_PREPARE_NO_VTAB                 0x04
+#define SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL                0x10
 
 /*
 ** CAPI3REF: Compiling An SQL Statement
 ** KEYWORDS: {SQL statement compiler}
 ** METHOD: sqlite3
 ** CONSTRUCTOR: sqlite3_stmt
 **
 ** To execute an SQL statement, it must first be compiled into a byte-code
 ** program using one of these routines.  Or, in other words, these routines
 ** are constructors for the [prepared statement] object.

fix_commit_message:
Add the SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL flag to sqlite3_prepare_v3(). Use this to prevent fts3/4 tables in non-trusted schemas from calling unsafe SQL functions.

findings.message: Commit 4b136ed70a marks the FTS3 virtual table as SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS (ext/fts3/fts3.c, fts3DeclareVtab), lowering its eVtabRisk to zero so that FTS3/4 tables can be created and used even when PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF (i.e. from untrusted/attacker-influenced schemas, such as those found in an attached or shared database). Before this change, SQLite's virtual-table risk checks (vtabIsReadOnly in src/delete.c, selectExpander in src/select.c) would block any access to FTS3/4 tables coming from an untrusted schema, so the module's internal SQL plumbing was never reachable in that threat model. After marking FTS3/4 innocuous, that protective gate disappears, but the module's internal SQL statements -- generated with sqlite3_mprintf() from schema-controlled strings (p->zName, p->zDb, p->zReadExprlist, p->zWriteExprlist, etc. -- see fts3SqlStmt in ext/fts3/fts3_write.c, fts3CursorSeekStmt/fts3FilterMethod in ext/fts3/fts3.c, fts3DoRebuild and sqlite3Fts3IntegrityCheck in ext/fts3/fts3_write.c) -- are still compiled via plain sqlite3_prepare_v2()/sqlite3_prepare_v3() calls with no indication that they originate from (and embed data governed by) a database schema. Because these statements are prepared as brand-new top-level Parse contexts, pParse->pToplevel is NULL and no Expr carries the EP_FromDDL/fromDDL flag, so the engine's existing 'disallow unsafe/DIRECTONLY SQL functions reached from untrusted schema content' checks in sqlite3ExprFunctionUsable (src/expr.c), vtabIsReadOnly (src/delete.c) and selectExpander (src/select.c) never trigger for them. The net effect is that an FTS3/4 virtual table defined inside a non-trusted schema can smuggle a call to an application-defined 'unsafe' SQL function into the engine, because the internal statements FTS3/4 prepares on its own behalf are never marked as DDL-derived and therefore are not subjected to the trusted-schema restriction, defeating the purpose of PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF / SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA.
findings.suggestion: Whenever a virtual table module (FTS3/4, FTS5, RTREE, or any other module marked SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS) prepares SQL statements on its own behalf using text assembled from schema-controlled identifiers, those statements must be prepared with a flag that marks them as schema/DDL-derived so the existing trusted-schema enforcement (sqlite3ExprFunctionUsable, vtabIsReadOnly, selectExpander) still applies to them. Concretely: add an SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL flag to sqlite3_prepare_v3(), thread it through Parse->prepFlags, and OR it into the trusted-schema checks (pParse->pToplevel!=0 in delete.c, pFrom->fg.fromDDL in select.c, ExprHasProperty(pExpr,EP_FromDDL) in expr.c) alongside the existing conditions; then update every internal fts3/fts3_write prepare call to go through a wrapper (e.g. sqlite3Fts3PrepareStmt) that always sets this flag.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: FTS3/4 internal SQL statements bypass trusted-schema protection against unsafe SQL functions

ground_truth.root_cause: SQLite's 'disallow unsafe SQL functions from untrasted schema content' protection was implemented by checking whether the current parse was a nested sub-parse of a top-level statement, or whether a specific expression was parsed directly from schema/DDL text. It did not account for virtual-table modules that, having been granted SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS status (and thus made usable from untrusted schemas), independently compile their own fresh top-level SQL statements built from schema-derived strings. Those internally-generated statements were indistinguishable, from the enforcement code's point of view, from ordinary trusted top-level user SQL, so the protection silently did not apply to them.

agent_reasoning: Without this guard, sqlite3VdbeTypeofColumn() is called unconditionally on the register returned by sqlite3ExprCodeTemp() in the TK_ISNULL/TK_NOTNULL codegen paths of sqlite3ExprIfTrue()/sqlite3ExprIfFalse(). When that register is a shared column-cache register (regFree1==0) rather than a fresh temp, tagging the preceding OP_Column with OPFLAG_TYPEOFARG permanently taints the cached register: on a later use of the same column (e.g. a CHECK constraint referencing the same NOT NULL/IS NULL column), OP_Column returns a pointer into the small fixed-size sqlite3CtypeMap[] array paired with the column's true (possibly huge) byte length instead of real data. A subsequent instruction like OP_MakeRecord then memcpy's using that bogus length, causing an out-of-bounds read past the 256-byte array and writing invalid data into the new record. Guarding the tagging with `if( regFree1 )` ensures only genuinely disposable temporaries are ever marked typeof-only, eliminating the unsound reuse; the added assert in OP_MakeRecord is a defensive backstop that would trip in debug builds if the sentinel pointer were ever copied as real data.

findings.message:
sqlite3ExprIfTrue()/sqlite3ExprIfFalse() code the IS NULL / IS NOT NULL operators by evaluating the operand into register r1 via sqlite3ExprCodeTemp(), then unconditionally call sqlite3VdbeTypeofColumn(v, r1). That helper (added in the same commit, src/vdbeaux.c) sets OPFLAG_TYPEOFARG on the immediately preceding OP_Column opcode if it targets r1, telling the VDBE that only the 'type' of the value is needed so it may skip loading large TEXT/BLOB content from overflow pages. When content is on overflow pages, OP_Column honors this flag (src/vdbe.c, OP_Column handler) by pointing the result Mem's z pointer at the global 256-byte array sqlite3CtypeMap[] while still setting Mem.n to the column's true (potentially much larger) declared length, since the real bytes are never meant to be read.

The bug is that sqlite3ExprCodeTemp() does not always allocate a fresh temporary register: when the operand is already a table column that is cached/reused elsewhere (e.g. the same column is later referenced by a CHECK constraint on that table), it can return r1 == the column's existing cache register with regFree1 == 0, meaning the register is NOT a disposable temp and its OP_Column instruction/result may be referenced again later for the column's real value. The code still unconditionally applied sqlite3VdbeTypeofColumn(v, r1) in this case, permanently marking the shared OP_Column with OPFLAG_TYPEOFARG. Consequently, when that same cached register was subsequently reused to obtain the actual column value (for example while evaluating a CHECK constraint containing NOT NULL/IS NULL on that column), the VDBE would deliver a Mem whose data pointer still referenced sqlite3CtypeMap with Mem.n set to the real (large) blob/string length rather than the genuine column bytes. Any later code path that treats this Mem as real content (e.g. OP_MakeRecord's memcpy(zPayload, pRec->z, pRec->n)) reads up to pRec->n bytes starting at the 256-byte sqlite3CtypeMap array -- an out-of-bounds read of adjacent process memory whose bytes are then copied into a database record, and invalid/incorrect data is used for the column.
findings.suggestion: Only apply the typeof-only optimization (sqlite3VdbeTypeofColumn) when the operand register r1 is a genuine disposable temporary allocated specifically for this IS NULL/NOT NULL test, i.e. when regFree1 is non-zero (and equals r1). If regFree1==0, the register is shared/cached and may later be read for its real value, so the preceding OP_Column must not be marked OPFLAG_TYPEOFARG.

pr_title: Proposed optimization to the IS NULL and NOT NULL operators that avoids loading the entire content of larges strings and BLOBs.  Response to [forum:/info/3c08d4715dc05b00

agent_reasoning: Without this change, nLocale, nText and nBlob are plain 32-bit ints. nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText is computed in 32-bit arithmetic and passed to sqlite3_malloc() (also 32-bit sized). On builds with an oversized SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH, an attacker supplying sufficiently large LOCALE/TEXT arguments could make nLocale+nText overflow a 32-bit int, wrapping to a small or negative value. sqlite3_malloc() would then allocate an undersized buffer, and the subsequent memcpy() calls (which use the original, non-overflowed i64-equivalent lengths) would write past the end of the allocation — a heap buffer overflow. Switching nLocale/nText/nBlob to i64 and using sqlite3_malloc64() ensures the size computation and allocation are performed with 64-bit precision, matching the real maximum sizes SQLite can represent, so the sum can no longer wrap and the allocation is always correctly sized for the subsequent copies.

findings.message: fts5LocaleFunc() (the implementation of the SQL function fts5_locale(LOCALE, TEXT)) declares nLocale, nText and nBlob as plain 'int' and computes nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText before allocating the result buffer with sqlite3_malloc(nBlob). sqlite3_value_bytes() returns an int whose value can approach SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH; when SQLite is built with an oversized SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH (a supported, documented compile-time option), the sum nLocale + 1 + nText can exceed INT_MAX and wrap around to a small or negative 'int' value. That truncated/wrapped value is then passed to sqlite3_malloc(), which allocates a buffer far smaller than the amount of data (nLocale and nText bytes) subsequently memcpy'd into it via memcpy(pBlob, zLocale, nLocale) and memcpy(&pBlob[nLocale+1], zText, nText), resulting in a heap buffer overflow. The bug requires a non-default build configuration (oversized SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH) to be reachable, since with the default SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH (1,000,000,000) the sum cannot overflow a 32-bit int.
findings.suggestion: Declare nLocale, nText and nBlob (and the analogous nBlob variable in the later refactored version of this function) as 64-bit (sqlite3_int64 / i64) instead of int, so that the addition nLocale + 1 + nText cannot wrap around a 32-bit boundary, and allocate with sqlite3_malloc64() (which accepts a 64-bit size) instead of sqlite3_malloc(). This matches the upstream fix, which widened the types and switched to sqlite3_malloc64().
findings.title: Integer overflow in fts5LocaleFunc() blob size computation

fix_commit.author: drh
fix_commit.message: Strengthen the fts5_locale() function against integer overflow attacks, even when SQLite is compiled with oversize values for SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Integer overflow in fts5LocaleFunc() blob size computation

ground_truth.root_cause: Lengths obtained from sqlite3_value_bytes() (an int, bounded in principle only by the compile-time SQLITE_MAX_LENGTH) are stored and summed using 32-bit 'int' arithmetic (nBlob = nLocale + 1 + nText) and then passed to the 32-bit-size-parameter sqlite3_malloc(), instead of using a 64-bit type and sqlite3_malloc64() throughout the computation and allocation.
